description: Hi everyone, we’re Vela, a team of students from NTU’s College of Computing and Data Science! We met through our orientation group, Vela 16.4, and this is our first hackathon together. Like the constellation named after a ship’s sails, we’re setting sail as a team for the very first time. Let’s see where the journey takes us!
summary:
Lunar Night Shift is an interactive web game where players manage a lunar habitat across 14-day solar day and night cycles in a full gameplay. It addresses STEM space learning challenges by converting complex engineering trade-offs—life support, battery storage, food production, water recycling, and radiation shielding—into intuitive turn-based decisions.

Across a 4-level campaign ("First Night", "Green Thumb", "Space Weather", and "The Big One"), players distribute solar energy to sustain life support, grow food in greenhouses, recycle water, run scientific laboratories, and charge batteries for the long night. Grounded in genuine NASA science, the game incorporates 2024 solar flare records from NASA's DONKI database and radiation readings from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter's CRaTER instrument. When solar storm alerts hit, players face realistic risk decisions: shelter the crew to avoid radiation at the cost of power and science, or stay active to advance research.

Lunar Night Shift is important because it connects real space telemetry with engaging gameplay, making mission survival, probability, and space hazards tangible for learners.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Lunar Night Shift is a web-based, turn-based survival strategy simulation where players step into the role of a lunar base commander. The game operates across alternating solar day and night cycles, requiring players to allocate generated solar power each turn into vital habitat subsystems—including Life Support (Oxygen), Greenhouse (Food Production), Water Recycling, Science Labs, Battery Storage, and Radiation Shielding.

The game features two distinct play modes:

  • Short Gameplay: Includes 3 levels lasting 8 turns each (4 day / 4 night) for introductory onboarding and faster play sessions.
  • Full Gameplay: A 4-level campaign—First Night, Green Thumb, Space Weather, and The Big One—spanning 14 turns per level (7 day / 7 night) to match real lunar orbital proportions.

During gameplay, live Solar Storm Alerts force critical risk-management decisions: commanders can shelter the crew to avoid radiation exposure at the cost of power and scientific output, or remain exposed to continue research while risking crew health. At the end of each level, an after-action report provides a 3-star performance rating, chronological event logs, telemetry charts tracking battery power against cosmic radiation spikes, and reflective discussion questions. If a mission fails the game offers strategic tips to help players iterate and retry.

2. What benefits does it have & what is its intended impact?

  • Benefits: It transforms abstract space architecture and environmental trade-offs into an intuitive, visual, and interactive strategy game. Rather than reading passive textbook descriptions, students actively experience the consequences of power scarcity, life support maintenance, and extreme environmental hazards.
  • Intended Impact: The project aims to bridge authentic space agency telemetry with engaging STEM education. By putting learners in charge of realistic risk scenarios, it fosters critical thinking, probability assessment, resource budgeting, and an interest in real-world space weather forecasting and lunar exploration.

3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Deployment & Web Platform: Developed as a responsive web application hosted on Netlify (heroic-axolotl-e2b768.netlify.app), making it instantly playable from standard web browsers on desktop, tablet, or mobile without installation.
  • Core Technologies: Built using standard front-end web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/UI frameworks) to manage turn state transitions, resource dashboard displays, and interactive decision controls.
  • Scientific Data Integration: Integrated open NASA space science archives, specifically historical May 2024 solar flare classifications from NASA’s DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, and Information) and radiation measurements from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) CRaTER instrument.

4. How is your project creative?

  • Data-Grounded Event Engine: Instead of relying on randomized game events, radiation surges and storm alerts are directly mapped to real 2024 NASA solar flare telemetry.
  • Realistic Energy Dynamics: The game mirrors actual lunar conditions by forcing players to hoard solar energy during the 7-day sunlit phase to survive the long, energy-draining 7-day lunar night strictly on battery reserves.
  • Educational Debrief Engine: End-level screens don't just display a score—they render comparative telemetry line graphs (battery storage vs. radiation intensity multiples) and pose reflective questions to turn gameplay into an active learning experience.

5. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scaffolding Learner Experience: Implemented both a Short Gameplay mode for beginners/quick classroom sessions and a Full Gameplay mode for deeper simulation.
  • Balancing Realism and Fun: Designed complex environmental factors (radiation exposure, battery storage limits, oxygen consumption, greenhouse growth costs) into clear, single-click daily allocations so the strategy remains accessible to young learners.
  • Constructive Failure: Ensured fail screens provide actionable feedback—explaining exactly why a base failed (e.g., running out of breathable air) alongside strategic tips—so players are encouraged to learn from mistakes.
